The items we need in writing: 1) exact BYOK workflow (import/export, wrapping algorithms, operator approvals), 2) expected maximum key lifetime and recommended rotation cadence by key class, and 3) TLS configurations for both control plane and data plane, including supported cipher suites and mTLS support for private deployments.

Subject: Re: Sec appendix follow-ups: key custody, rotation, and TLS profile

Samantha —

Thanks for the clear asks. We're drafting a short control mapping and an operational runbook now. High-level answers up front while we attach the artifacts:

- BYOK workflow: Customer uploads wrapped key material via our private import API; import requires HSM-wrapped key at rest, a signed import request (customer KMS signature), and a two-person operator approval inside the Private control plane. We support RSA-OAEP and AES-KWP wrapping for import/export.
- Key rotation: We classify keys as Master (KMK), Data-encryption keys (DEK), and Session/ephemeral. Recommended rotation: KMK annually (or on key compromise), DEK every 90 days (or on model rollout), ephemeral per session. We support automated rotation policies and manual rotation with zero-downtime rewrap.
- TLS: Control plane uses mTLS with TLS1.3 preferred; data plane endpoints support TLS1.2 and TLS1.3 (ECDHE-based cipher suites only). We provide a cipher list and evidence in the attachments.

I'll attach the control mapping spreadsheet and the operational runbook (step-by-step import, rotation, and emergency key-escrow procedures). Aditya and Neha will add technical details and SOC2 evidence pointers.

Will send attachments in the next email.

Thanks,

Samantha / team —

Attaching the two artifacts you requested: the control mapping spreadsheet (tabbed by requirement -> Redwood control -> evidence) and the operational runbook PDF. A few clarifying notes to call out from the tech side:

1) BYOK import flow: We do not persist customer unwrapped key material on our systems. Customers must wrap with their own KMS/HSM before transport. Import transaction metadata is logged to our audit service (immutable append-only ledger) with KMS key-id references, operator ids, and timestamp. You can request a redacted audit export for procurement review.

2) HSM model support: For Private deployments we support HSMs compatible with PKCS#11 (Gemalto/Thales and AWS CloudHSM). For Hosted, Redwood uses an HSM-backed key hierarchy managed by Redwood (SOC2 controls apply; see evidence tab).

3) Rotation & rewrap: Rotation is implemented as rewrap with dual-write to new key and progressive cut-over. We provide a test harness for your SREs to validate rewrap without traffic impact.

I've included a short sample cURL for the import API in the runbook.

-Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-kms-control-mapping.xlsx, redwood-kms-runbook-v1.2.pdf

Aditya / Mateo —

Received the artifacts and ran them past our security SME. A couple of clarifications before we mark this closed: 1) For on-prem/private deployments, what is the operator approval UX? Is the second approval performed by customer admins or Redwood personnel? 2) In the runbook the sample import cURL references a "signed import request" — can you give the exact header/claim set we need to produce from our KMS so engineers can script it? 3) Can you confirm whether TLS mutual authentication can be enforced on data-plane endpoints for Private deployments (we need mTLS enforced between our VPC and the redwood node)?

We'd prefer customer-controlled operator approvals and mandatory mTLS on the data plane for Private installs.

Thanks — Samantha

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@amplehealth.com>, mateo_alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Sec appendix follow-ups: key custody, rotation, and TLS profile

Samantha — good questions, quick answers and next steps: 

1) Operator approvals: For Private deployments we support customer-managed operator approvals. The control plane offers role-based approval flows; customers can configure "Customer-only" approval mode so Redwood operators are never in the approval path. We'll include configuration screenshots in the runbook.

2) Signed import request: The signed import request is a JSON Web Signature (JWS) where the payload includes import_key_id, wrapping_algorithm, key_type, key_length, timestamp, and a nonce. The header must indicate alg=RS256 and include your KMS public key thumbprint. Example claim set (single-line) is included in section 3 of the runbook; the import API validates the signature against the public key you upload during onboarding.

3) Data-plane mTLS: Confirmed — for Private deployments mTLS can be enforced on data-plane endpoints. You can supply your client certificate chain and CA during onboarding and we bind it to your tenant. We will document the exact steps (cert format, rotation guidance) in the runbook appendix.

Next steps: I'll update the runbook with the explicit JWS claim example and add the operator approval UI screenshots. Mateo will share the updated files to the SharePoint link and we can close the ticket once Ample Health accepts the mapping.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Security Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
